content:
Apple has applied for a temporary restraining order in its ongoing trade secrets lawsuit against OpenAI. Apple said it would suffer "irreparable harm" from the alleged theft of its trade secrets if the order is not granted.

In its application, Apple said it wrote to OpenAI after filing its initial lawsuit last month, stating its intention to "seek temporary injunctive relief." However, Apple said it would not take legal action if OpenAI agreed to five demands:

  • Stop accessing or using Apple's confidential information
  • Stop any ongoing use or disclosure
  • Preserve all evidence
  • Allow forensic inspection of devices, cloud storage, email, Slack, Teams, and other databases
  • Search OpenAI's systems for any confidential information belonging to Apple

Apple said OpenAI has agreed to the first three demands, but the two sides have not reached consensus on the last two.

Apple is therefore asking the court to issue a temporary restraining order, directing a judge to immediately bar OpenAI from using or obtaining any Apple trade secrets, preserve all evidence, allow Apple to conduct forensic inspections of OpenAI's devices and accounts, and return any Apple confidential information still in OpenAI's possession.

Apple said:

Separately, Apple has also filed a motion asking the court to expedite discovery, including earlier production of documents and taking depositions of OpenAI's key employees and management out of court.

Alongside Apple's filing, OpenAI issued its longest public response yet to Apple's lawsuit. In a blog post published late at night, OpenAI said the "reckless, combative and deeply personal" lawsuit was at odds with Apple's image as "one of the greatest companies in history."

The hearing on the restraining order is scheduled for October 1, 2026. The full filing is available below.
